title: Agent Explorative Policy Optimization for Agentic Multimodal Reasoning
claim: Our method beats the standard training baseline at every scale, and a smaller model with it matches or surpasses a much larger untrained one.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, callout boxes with dashed arrows on right
description: Two side-by-side line charts share an x-axis of model size on a log scale (2B, 4B, 8B, 32B). The left panel plots average Pass@1 and the right plots average Pass@4. Each panel has four lines: grey for the untrained base, light salmon for SFT, red for SFT+GRPO, and a thick dark blue for SFT+AXPO (ours). The base line is the only one that continues to 32B. The blue line sits on top at every size, and its endpoint values are bolded (62.3, 75.8). The right panel has two boxed callouts joined by dashed curved arrows. One reads 'AXPO 2B ≈ Base 8B' and the other reads 'AXPO 8B > Base 32B', both marked '4× fewer parameters'. A shared legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the blue line and the callouts.
caption: Main result: AXPO narrows the agentic gap to a 4× larger baseline. Average Pass@1 (left) and Pass@4 (right) over nine multimodal benchmarks across Qwen3-VL-Thinking sizes. At 8B, AXPO
abstract: Vision-language models with extended reasoning succeed on complex problems, but many real-world problems require external tools that internal reasoning alone often cannot resolve. Agentic reasoning therefore interleaves two behaviors with a structural asymmetry: thinking (the self-contained default) and tool use (a high-variance auxiliary acting). We refer to this asymmetry as the Thinking-Acting Gap. Under standard RL recipes like GRPO, the gap manifests as two diagnostic symptoms during training: tool use is attempted on only ~30% of rollouts, and when attempted, the tool-using rollouts within a group are all-wrong on ~40% of questions, suppressing the learning signal at the tool calls that needed it. We propose AXPO (Agent eXplorative Policy Optimization): for each all-wrong tool-using subgroup, AXPO fixes the thinking prefix and resamples the tool call and its continuation, paired with uncertainty-based prefix selection. Across nine multimodal benchmarks and three scales of Qwen3-VL-Thinking, SFT+AXPO outperforms SFT+GRPO at average (+1.8pp Pass@1 and +1.8pp Pass@4 at 8B on average) and 8B with SFT+AXPO surpasses the 32B Base on Pass@4 with 4x fewer parameters.
